corrected_content.worked_solution: The field has potential $\phi=(x^2+y^2+z^2)/2$. At the initial point, $\phi=1/2$; at $t=\pi$, $\phi=(1+4\pi)/2$. Hence $$\int_C F\cdot dr=\phi(r(\pi))-\phi(r(0))=2\pi.$$ Equivalently $F(r(t))\cdot r'(t)=2$ for $t>0$; its integral has the same finite limit at $t=0$.
